correctness.rationale: A seed distance d reaches sentinel j with probability p^d and delay exactly d. Hence detection probability F_j/(n-1) and conditional mean μ_j=pF_j'/F_j. Moving inward replaces p^(n-j) with p^j; the comparison has sign M_j−μ_j where M_j=j−(n−2j)p^(n−2j)/(1−p^(n−2j)). The log-parameter derivative of μ_j is a strictly positive conditional variance while M_j decreases strictly from j to −infinity, giving one adjacent crossing for each nonendpoint j. Since x/2*coth(λx/2) strictly increases, M_(j+1)>M_j whenever both are defined, proving τ_j<τ_(j+1) and the global centerward ordering. n=5 cross polynomial p²+2p−1. Analytic argument proves all n≥3, all 0<p<1. A packaged standard-library verifier enumerates exact edge states for n2..9 and checks rational threshold ordering to n24; certificate matches its output. Risk: genuine epidemiological models with delays/repeated transmission are out of scope.

originality.rationale: The four inspected primary studies establish the sentinel motivation and, in Holme 2017, explicitly the conditional-time objective; neither this objective nor its elementary weighted-distance formula is claimed as new. Their empirical and continuous-time epidemic models do not imply the complete all-n threshold order on homogeneous paths with deterministic crossing times. Two closest published search hits concerned discounted complete-bipartite hitting domination and normalized-path dynamical sampling, neither of which entails the claim; two closest accessible past results concerned vaccination sites or two-seed influence, also distinct. This supports best-knowledge originality, with residual equivalence risk in exponential tilting/distance-polynomial literature.

value.rationale: This solves the natural speed-versus-coverage surveillance location problem on every finite path for a single conditional-detection metric, with exactly one threshold per interior candidate, strict ordering of thresholds, a nonempty optimality interval for every possible monitoring site, and a sharp five-vertex first-change boundary. The distinction between conditional speed and unconditional coverage is decision-relevant; it is a structural infinite-family classification rather than a finite table, trivial substitution or an asserted empirical efficacy claim.
